summary:
ITV Anglia is ITV’s regional service for eastern England, based in Norwich and owned by ITV plc. It serves areas including Norfolk, Suffolk, Essex and Cambridgeshire, with regional news produced in two editions.

Anglia Television launched on 27 October 1959 as an independent ITV franchise. It became known for drama and the nature series *Survival*, and retained its franchise in 1980 and 1991. From 1994, it passed through a series of media-company acquisitions before Granada and Carlton merged to form ITV plc in 2004. Anglia then ceased to operate as a separate brand, though the regional service continued as ITV Anglia.

The station’s Norwich headquarters remain at Anglia House. Its former Magdalen Street studios were sold in 2006 and became a centre for creative businesses. Anglia’s best-known on-screen symbol was a silver knight, later replaced by corporate ITV branding. Much of its programme archive is preserved at the East Anglian Film Archive.
